title: Bridged-burst handshake decay causing throttled warm-starts across hosted/dedicated/private
creator: Aisha Verma
description:
Summary: Multiple paying customers on Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported sustained 429s and degraded throughput during traffic warm-ups and post-deploy rollouts. The root cause was a race in burst token ledger reconciliation during policy migrations and control-plane handoffs: an epoch mismatch allowed proxies to treat stale burst snapshots as authoritative, causing a temporary negative credit surface and aggressive throttling. The issue affected canary and full rollouts where policy versions were staggered across regions.

Scope & Impact: Several enterprise tenants experienced 5-30 minute windows of opaque throttles (429s) on normal traffic patterns; observed impact included inference latency spikes, increased retries from client SDKs, and customer escalations to SRE/CS. Impacted environments: hosted API (multi-region), dedicated GPU pools for two customers, and one Private on-prem deployment undergoing an autoscaler upgrade.

Observed signals:
- Sudden rise in tenant-level 429s coincident with policy-migration jobs (control plane logs show burst_policy:v2 rollouts).
- Discrepancy between control-plane ledger snapshot epochs and proxy-held epoch in /metrics/burst_epoch.<epoch>.
- Admission logs showing credits_applied = negative for short windows.
- Spike in orchestrator reconciliation latency during leader handoff.
- Support tickets: INC-57842, INC-57901.

Root cause: During policy migration we write a serialized burst_state to the tenant ledger with an epoch marker. Proxies accept the first ledger update they see and set local burst windows accordingly. Under a particular sequence of events (leader failover + staggered policy rollout + slight clock skew), a delayed but later-applied ledger write contained a lower epoch value (due to a restore-from-snapshot path) which the proxy mistakenly accepted, rolling back local credits. The reconciliation logic lacked an idempotent compare-and-swap and had insufficient guards for out-of-order epoch application.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Rolled back the migration to the previous consistent policy in affected regions.
- Enabled emergency bypass for legacy-quota-marker on impacted proxies to accept only monotonic epoch increases (temporary enforcement toggle).
- Hand-applied tenant ledgers for 3 high-value customers using a reconciliation script to restore credits and cleared support escalations.

Permanent fix implemented:
- Patch: add CAS-based ledger write path with strict epoch monotonicity checks and validation in the proxy apply path (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/4823).
- Migration orchestration change: ensure control-plane publishes a migration-complete marker and waits for cross-region probe-confirmation before deprecating old policy version.
- Orchestrator improvement: reduce leader handoff window by making lease renewal earlier and add a backoff jitter to avoid synchronized snapshot restores.
- Add unit and e2e tests that simulate out-of-order ledger application and leader failover.

Telemetry & Alerts added:
- New metric: tenant_burst_epoch_mismatch{tenant} with alert on >1% of tenant requests seeing epoch regressions.
- Histogram for credits_applied per-request and alert when negative credits observed.
- Dashboard: New Quota Health page showing epoch delta, last_applied_ledger_ts, and reconciliation latency per-tenant.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary runtime-1.19.2 with CAS patch to 10% of proxies in one region for 24h.
2) Run cross-region probes simulating heavy warm-up traffic and validate no regressions.
3) Gradual 25/50/100% rollout with automated safety gating.

Backfill & follow-ups:
- Backfill script written to reconcile tenant ledgers for window 2025-02-14T00:00..2025-02-15T12:00 (script: tools/reconcile_burst_ledger.sh).
- Postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-230112+-+burst+ledger+handshake+decay.
- Customer communication: templated incident post and targeted emails drafted by CS (CS-communication-ENG-230112.md).

Open action items:
- [ ] Finish canary rollout and collect 72-hour telemetry (owner: Marcus Lee).
- [ ] Run chaos tests to validate leader failover safe path (owner: Platform-Resilience).
- [ ] Add a safety net in console to surface per-tenant epoch deltas to SREs (owner: Console team).
- [ ] Schedule a security review for ledger serialization changes if needed (owner: Security).

Notes: This ticket ties into long-running work on quota stability and burst behaviour (see project quota-and-burst-stability). Coordination required with Dedicated ops and Private deployment POC to ensure on-prem upgrades include the CAS-enabled runtime.
comments: 2025-02-15: Incident first detected by paging rules after CS reports customer INC-57842. Initial triage points to policy migration around 08:12 UTC.
2025-02-15: Marcus migrated 3 customers back to policy v1 as emergency rollback; observed immediate reduction in 429 spike.
2025-02-17: Patch development complete; integration tests added to proxy repo. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/4823
2025-02-20: Canary started in us-west-2; early telemetry shows no epoch regressions in canary cohort.
2025-02-26: Reconciliation backfill run for affected window; scripts validated and customers notified.
2025-02-28: Preparing release notes for runtime-1.19.2 and scheduling rollout.
